My name is from the North East, and I farm sorghum on this 1.71 hectare plot near my home. The rains here are short, only coming from June to September, so I must plant quickly when they start. I have some schooling and a bigger farm of almost 8 hectares total, so I can afford a little fertilizer — I will buy some urea and NPK if the subsidy reaches our area, but not too much because sorghum does not need as much as maize. I will use my own seed I saved from last year because improved sorghum seed is hard to find from the agro-dealers here, and I will rely on my family and one or two hired hands during weeding and harvest.
